stories.title: Schema v0 — `ops_settings`, `ops_client`, `ops_placement`, `ops_timesheet`, `ops_timesheet_entry`, `ops_timesheet_event` (+ JPA, repositories)
stories.depsNote: O1.1 org core schema (org_member is the consultant identity), O1.4 org_audit_event. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As the API, I want the additive timesheet tables so that every later story has a home and OrgIsolationIT has routes to discover.
stories.genz: Six tables, org_id first on every one, no column that could ever hold an SSN.
ac: Liquibase changeset `20261013010000_ts_skeleton.xml` (included from `master.xml`) creates `ops_settings`, `ops_client`, `ops_placement`, `ops_timesheet`, `ops_timesheet_entry`, `ops_timesheet_event` exactly as DESIGN §5.1, §5.2, §5.4, §5.6, §5.7, §5.9 (rates, vendors, holidays, attachments, prefs, consent arrive in later stories); every table `org_id` first; MySQL 8 utf8mb4, DATETIME(6) UTC; `ops_timesheet.live_key` is a generated STORED UNIQUE column `IF(status IN ('DRAFT','SUBMITTED','APPROVED'), CONCAT(placement_id,':',week_start), NULL)`.

JPA entities under `domain/org/ops/` (`OpsSettings`, `OpsClient`, `OpsPlacement`, `OpsTimesheet`, `OpsTimesheetEntry`, `OpsTimesheetEvent`), enums `OpsTimesheetStatus {DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, SUPERSEDED}`, `OpsDayKind {WORK, PTO, HOLIDAY, SICK, UNPAID}`, `OpsEntrySource {MANUAL, COPIED, PREFILL, OCR}`, `OpsPlacementStatus {ACTIVE, ON_HOLD, ENDED}`, `OpsPayTypeLabel {W2, X1099, C2C, OTHER}`; repositories expose `findByIdAndOrgId` on every entity (no finder without org_id).

No column in any `ops_*` table matches the never-collected deny-list regex (`ssn|itin|ein|tax_id|routing|account_no|account_number|iban|swift|passport|visa|i94|i9|dob|birth|home_address|salary`); `pay_type_label` is an enum column, not free text.
`AccountDeletionService` and `AccountExportService` gain TODO hooks naming H7.2 (no behaviour yet) so the GDPR suites still pass.
stories.tech: `api/src/main/resources/config/liquibase/changelog/20261013010000_ts_skeleton.xml`, `api/src/main/java/com/dossier/api/domain/org/ops/*`, `repository/org/ops/*`. Note: `service/ops/` already exists for platform ops (ErrorDigest) - consultancy ops lives under `org/ops/` everywhere.
stories.tests: `TimesheetsSchemaIT` (Testcontainers MySQL): inserts/reads each entity; `live_key` uniqueness - a second DRAFT for the same placement+week fails, a SUPERSEDED row does not; a column-name deny-list test over the changelog (seed of H3.1's `OpsNeverCollectedTest`).

stories.title: FINANCE role + `ops.*` permissions, pilot gate (flag + opsPilot), `ops_settings` GET/PATCH
stories.depsNote: H0.1; O1.2 OrgAccessService (the FINANCE value is already in the enum); A5.3 flags; A5.1 settings registry for the defaults. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As the team, I want the FINANCE role live and the module invisible until a platform admin switches a pilot org on.
stories.genz: Finance stays with finance; consultants see their own hours; nobody else sees the module exists.
ac: `OrgPermission` gains `ops.settings`, `ops.placements`, `ops.timesheets.approve`, `ops.timesheets.own`, `ops.finance` per tenant-model.md §4: OWNER/ADMIN/FINANCE hold the first three and `ops.finance`; MEMBER holds `ops.timesheets.own` only while they have ≥ 1 placement (computed, not stored); MARKETER/STAFF hold none.

Gate: every `/api/orgs/{id}/ops/**` handler is `@OrgPermissionRequired` and additionally passes `OpsGate.require(orgId)`: flag `flag.ops_timesheets` (A5.3, default off) must be on AND (`organization.settings_json.opsPilot = true` OR, once H7.1 lands, `EntitlementService.hasOrg(orgId, 'ops.enabled')`); otherwise 404 when the flag is off and 402 `PLAN_REQUIRED {feature: 'ops.enabled'}` when only the org lacks it. The platform-admin action that sets `opsPilot` is `AdminOrgResource POST /api/admin/orgs/{id}/ops-pilot` (audited HIGH).

`GET/PATCH /api/orgs/{id}/ops/settings` (`ops.settings`): fields per DESIGN §5.1; defaults come from settings `org.ops.week_start_default` (1), `org.ops.step_minutes_default` (15), `org.ops.expected_hours_tolerance_pct` (10), `org.ops.long_day_hours` (12), `org.ops.proof_required_default` (true), `org.ops.retention_min_years` (7, hard minimum 7); `retentionYears` below the minimum → 422; `weekStart` change with live DRAFT/SUBMITTED sheets → 409 `LIVE_SHEETS`; `ocrEnabled` default false (D7); `approvalRequired` default true (D9); the row is created on first read.
Feature registry entry `timesheets` (A5.7) declares the global switch, the per-org switch and the typed limits so an unregistered gate fails `FeatureRegistryTest`.
stories.tech: `domain/org/OrgPermission.java` (O1.2), `service/org/ops/OpsGate.java`, `service/org/ops/OpsSettingsService.java`, `web/rest/org/ops/OpsSettingsResource.java`, `web/rest/AdminOrgResource.java` (pilot action), `service/AdminAuditService.java` (existing) for the HIGH audit row.
stories.tests: `OpsRoleMatrixTest` skeleton (FINANCE/ADMIN/OWNER/MEMBER-with-placement/MEMBER-without/MARKETER/STAFF × every permission); `OpsGateTest` (flag off → 404, flag on + no pilot → 402, pilot → 200, entitlement path stubbed); `OpsSettingsResourceIT` (defaults from the registry, 422 below retention minimum, 409 on week-start change with live sheets).
stories.benchmark: Ceipal WorkForce has a 25-user minimum; Bullhorn T&E is quote-based with enterprise setup. Ours: a flag and one admin tap puts a five-person shop on the module.

stories.title: Placements-lite API — client inline, consultant × client × start date, `/mine`, no rates
stories.depsNote: H0.2; O2.2 email invites (consultants must be org members; the picker reads GET /members from O1.3/O2.2). Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As finance, I want to say who is placed where from when, in one call, so that the consultant's first sheet can appear.
stories.genz: Consultant + client + date. That is the whole setup.
ac: `POST /api/orgs/{id}/ops/placements` (`ops.placements`) accepts `{consultantMemberId, clientId | newClientName, title?, startDate, endDate?, hoursPerWeekExpected?, proofRequired?, payTypeLabel?}`; `newClientName` creates the `ops_client` row inline (unique `(org_id, name)`, 409 `CLIENT_EXISTS` on a case-insensitive clash); `hoursPerWeekExpected` defaults to setting `org.ops.expected_hours_default` (40); `proofRequired` inherits `ops_settings.proof_required_default`; the consultant must be an ACTIVE org member → else 422 `MEMBER_NOT_ACTIVE`.

`GET /ops/placements?consultantMemberId&clientId&status`, `PATCH /ops/placements/{id}` (title, dates, status, proofRequired, hoursPerWeekExpected), `GET /ops/clients`, `POST /ops/clients`, `PATCH /ops/clients/{id}`, `POST /ops/clients/{id}/archive`; `GET /ops/placements/mine` returns the caller's own placements (client name, title, dates, expected hours only).

Every String field on every request DTO is annotated `@NoSensitiveText` (interim: the shared `SensitivePatterns` from T1.1 or a local copy with the same rules until H3.1 moves it product-wide) → 422 `SENSITIVE_CONTENT` with the message 'Don't put account, tax, ID-document numbers or dates of birth here — we never collect them.'
Audit: `OPS_PLACEMENT_CREATE/UPDATE/END` and `OPS_CLIENT_*` rows via `OrgAuditService` (O1.4) with the consultant login as target; foreign org id → 404 on every verb.
stories.tech: `service/org/ops/{OpsClientService,OpsPlacementService}.java`, `web/rest/org/ops/{OpsClientResource,OpsPlacementResource}.java`, `service/org/ops/dto/*`. Rates, vendors and holidays are H1.1/H1.2 - leave `vendor_id` nullable and unused here.
stories.tests: `OpsPlacementResourceIT` (create with inline client, 409 clash, 422 inactive member, 404 foreign org, `/mine` own-only); `OpsPlacementDtoTest` (reflection: no bill/pay field exists on any DTO in this story; every String field annotated); `OrgIsolationIT` (O1.5) discovers the new routes without wiring.
stories.benchmark: Bullhorn T&E requires placement data to be perfect in the ATS before approval (Bullhorn KB payroll workflow). Ours: consultant + client + date; everything else optional.

stories.title: Weekly sheet core v0 — current-week DRAFT, whole-week PUT (WORK minutes), submit, approve, reject → DRAFT, own-only, audit
stories.depsNote: H0.3. Size L. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want my week to exist and be submittable; as finance, I want to approve or send it back with a comment.
stories.genz: Draft → submitted → approved. Reject gives it back as a draft with the note, never a locked screen.
ac: `GET /ops/timesheets/current` (consultant): for each ACTIVE placement returns the live sheet for the current org week, creating a DRAFT prefilled with `hours_per_week_expected ÷ 5` on weekdays (`source=PREFILL`) when none exists; `week_start` is the org week-start weekday in `organization.timezone` (422 `WEEK_START_INVALID` otherwise); `POST /ops/timesheets {placementId, weekStart}` for an explicit week → 409 `TIMESHEET_EXISTS` when a live one exists.

`PUT /ops/timesheets/{id}/entries` (DRAFT only, else 409 `NOT_DRAFT`): whole-week replace `[{day, kind: WORK, minutes, note?}]` with minutes a multiple of `ops_settings.step_minutes`, 0–1440 per day; recomputes `work_minutes`/`total_minutes`; `source=MANUAL`. Day kinds other than WORK are H2.1.

`POST .../submit` → SUBMITTED (422 `DAY_OVER_24H` when any day > 1440; 422 `EMPTY_SHEET` when total is 0); `POST .../approve` (`ops.timesheets.approve`) → APPROVED with `decided_at`/`decided_by_member_id`; own sheet → 409 `SELF_APPROVAL` unless `ops_settings.approval_required=false` (D9; then the sheet carries `self_recorded=true`); `POST .../reject {comment ≤ setting org.ops.reject_comment_max_chars (500)}` → DRAFT with `last_rejection_comment`; `GET /ops/timesheets?weekStart&status&consultantMemberId&placementId&page` (approver: all; consultant: the service forces `consultantMemberId = me`); `GET /ops/timesheets/{id}` with entries and events.

APPROVED rows are immutable: no endpoint touches their entries (PUT → 409 `NOT_DRAFT`); every mutation appends `ops_timesheet_event` (CREATED, PREFILLED, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED) and mirrors `OPS_TS_SUBMIT/APPROVE/REJECT` into `org_audit_event` through one `OpsAuditService`; a consultant reading another consultant's sheet gets 404.
stories.tech: `service/org/ops/{OpsTimesheetService,OpsWeekCalendar,OpsAuditService}.java`, `web/rest/org/ops/OpsTimesheetResource.java`, DTOs under `service/org/ops/dto/`. Withdraw, correction, locks and the flags table are H2.2/H2.3 - keep the state enum complete (SUPERSEDED exists, unused).
stories.tests: `OpsTimesheetStateTest` (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED, reject→DRAFT keeps the comment, PUT after approve 409, SELF_APPROVAL 409 vs approval_required=false); `OpsWeekCalendarTest` (week_start by org timezone and DST boundary, Monday/Sunday starts); `OpsTimesheetResourceIT` (current creates prefilled draft once, concurrent create hits live_key → one 409, consultant own-only 404, audit row per mutation).
stories.benchmark: SAP Fieldglass / Beeline rejections and locked sheets need the program office (SAP KB 3756050, Beeline worker guide). Ours: reject returns an editable draft with the comment.

stories.title: Consultant week view v0 (`/timesheets`, 390 px) + approver inbox v0 (`/org/ops/timesheets`)
stories.depsNote: H0.4; O1.6 web gate ((org)/layout.tsx on /api/orgs/mine with role redirects). Size L. Owner web + ui.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want to open the week, fix a number and submit from my phone; as finance, I want a list I can approve from.
stories.genz: Open, glance, tap submit. The approver clears a list with a thumb.
ac: `/timesheets` in the user app (route group `(app)`, so the file is `web/src/app/(app)/timesheets/page.tsx` - there is no `/app/` segment): week header with ‹ › navigation and a placement switcher only when > 1 placement; seven day rows with − / + steppers (≥ 44 px targets, step = `ops_settings.step_minutes`); total vs expected line; Submit (disabled at 0 minutes); after submit the card flips read-only with status; after a reject the comment shows at the top of the DRAFT. Reads/writes go through the web BFF (`web/src/lib/api.ts` pattern) with the ETag-free whole-week PUT.

`/org/ops/timesheets` in the org console (`web/src/app/(org)/org/ops/timesheets/page.tsx`): Pending list (consultant · client · week · total) with Approve and Reject (comment required, ≤ 500); role-gated by `ops.timesheets.approve`; the module link appears in the org nav only when the gate passes (`GET /api/orgs/{id}/ops/settings` 200).

stories.title: GENERIC CSV export v0 — synchronous, FINANCE and consultant self-export, audited
stories.depsNote: H0.4. Size S. Owner API.
stories.story: As finance, I want approved hours out as a CSV on day one so the pilot shops never feel locked in.
stories.genz: One tap, one file, no export tax.
ac: `GET /ops/timesheets/export?from&to&consultantMemberId?&format=CSV` (`ops.timesheets.approve`) streams the GENERIC layout per DESIGN §9 (org, consultant display name + member id, client, placement title, week_start, day, kind, minutes, hours 2 dp, note, status, approved_at, approved_by, flags) as UTF-8 with BOM; rows capped at setting `org.ops.export_sync_rows_max` (default 5 000) → 413 `EXPORT_TOO_LARGE` with the hint to use the async export (H5.1).
`GET /ops/timesheets/mine/export?from&to&format=CSV` for consultants: own sheets only, no pay columns.

`OpsExportColumns` registry (one place that names the columns per layout) with a unit test asserting no column name contains the deny-list tokens (`ssn|itin|ein|tax|routing|account|iban|swift|passport|visa|i94|i9|dob|birth|address|salary`).
Audit `OPS_EXPORT` per file with layout, period, row count and sha256.
stories.tests: `OpsExportTest` (GENERIC columns vs fixture, BOM, 2-dp hours, cap → 413, consultant own-only, audit row with sha256); `OpsExportColumnsDenyListTest`.
stories.benchmark: Harvest/Clockify export generic CSV at every tier; Conrep/Ceipal tie exports to their own invoicing. Ours: open CSV from the first week.

stories.title: Vendors + effective-dated rate history — `ops_vendor`, `ops_placement_rate`, minor units, FINANCE-only, pay-visibility switch
stories.depsNote: H0.7 (skeleton proven). Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As finance, I want the bill and pay rate in force for any week, changed mid-placement without rewriting history, and never shown to the wrong person.
stories.genz: Rates are dated rows, not a field you overwrite. Consultants never see the bill side.
ac: Changeset `20261013020000_ts_rates_holidays.xml` adds `ops_vendor` (DESIGN §5.3) and `ops_placement_rate` (§5.5: `effective_from DATE`, `bill_rate_minor INT NULL`, `pay_rate_minor INT NULL`, unique `(placement_id, effective_from)`), plus `ops_holiday` (§5.10, used by H1.2).

`POST /ops/placements/{id}/rates {effectiveFrom, billRateMinor?, payRateMinor?}` (`ops.finance`); `OpsRateService.inForce(placementId, weekStart)` returns the latest row with `effective_from ≤ week_start`; `PATCH /ops/placements/{id}` accepts `vendorName` (creates/links an `ops_vendor` row); money is integer minor units in `ops_settings.currency` (one per org); no floats anywhere.

Visibility: `bill_rate_minor` and vendor chain are absent from every consultant and marketer DTO by construction (separate DTO classes, not a null field); `pay_rate_minor` appears on the consultant's own placement/sheet DTOs only when `ops_settings.show_pay_to_consultant=true`; `OPS_RATE_SET` audit rows record 'set' and the effective date, never the amount.
`@NoSensitiveText` on vendor/client contact fields; `ops_client.contact_email` is a business contact, documented as such in the DTO.
stories.tests: `OpsRateServiceTest` (rate in force by week incl. same-day change, none before first effective date); `OpsPayVisibilityTest` (reflection over consultant/marketer DTOs: no field named *bill*; pay field present only with the switch); `OpsPlacementResourceIT` extended (FINANCE-only on rates, 404 for MEMBER).
stories.benchmark: Conrep stores bill/pay rate per placement (vendor side) with no consultant view. Ours: effective-dated, FINANCE-only, and the consultant may be shown their own pay rate by an org switch.

stories.title: Holidays (seeded list by country, editable) + placement lifecycle — ON_HOLD / ENDED, end-date guard, trailing weeks
stories.depsNote: H1.1 (table). Size S. Owner API.
stories.story: As finance, I want holidays to pre-set a day and a placement's end date to stop new weeks without losing trailing hours.
stories.genz: Holidays suggest, never force. Ending a placement does not delete anyone's last week.
ac: `GET/POST/DELETE /ops/holidays` (`ops.settings`); on first settings read for an org with `organization.country = 'US'` the list named by setting `org.ops.holiday_seed` (default `US_FEDERAL`, a registry of lists in code keyed by country) is seeded once (idempotent); holidays only pre-set the day kind in H2.1, never a value.

`PATCH /ops/placements/{id} {status: ON_HOLD|ENDED, endDate}`: ENDED/ON_HOLD placements drop out of `GET /current` auto-creation; moving `end_date` earlier than an existing APPROVED/SUBMITTED week → 409 `SHEETS_AFTER_END {weeks[]}`; weeks after `end_date` can be created only by an approver (`POST /ops/timesheets` with `ops.timesheets.approve`) and carry the `AFTER_END_DATE` flag (H2.2).

'Active consultant' definition lives in one query (`OpsPlacementRepository.countActiveConsultants(orgId, from, to)`): a member with ≥ 1 placement `ACTIVE` during the period - H7.1 bills from it, H3.3/H3.4 budgets multiply by it.
stories.tests: `OpsHolidaySeedTest` (seed once, country gate, delete survives re-read); `OpsPlacementLifecycleTest` (409 on earlier end date with sheets, auto-create stops, approver-only trailing week); `countActiveConsultants` fixture test.

stories.title: Day kinds (PTO / HOLIDAY / SICK / UNPAID), step minutes, day notes, copy-last-week, prefill from last approved week
stories.depsNote: H0.7; H1.2 holidays. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want PTO and holidays recorded and my next week to start from my last one.
stories.genz: Copied from last week - tap to change. Most weeks you change nothing.
ac: `PUT /ops/timesheets/{id}/entries` accepts kinds `WORK|PTO|HOLIDAY|SICK|UNPAID`; a day may hold one row per kind (unique `(timesheet_id, day, kind)`); per-kind minute totals (`work_minutes`, `pto_minutes`, ...) recomputed; only WORK is billable; `note` ≤ setting `org.ops.note_max_chars` (200) with `@NoSensitiveText`.

Prefill on auto-create: last APPROVED sheet for the placement (same minutes per weekday, kinds reset to WORK, notes cleared, `source=PREFILL`), else `expected ÷ 5`; `POST .../copy-last-week` copies minutes and kinds from the previous week's latest live sheet (`source=COPIED`); org holidays in the week pre-set `HOLIDAY` with 0 WORK minutes - overridable by the consultant.
Sheet DTO carries `prefilledFrom: LAST_WEEK|EXPECTED|NONE` and the holiday names per day so the UI can label them.
stories.tests: `OpsPrefillTest` (last approved → copied; none → expected ÷ 5; holiday pre-set; kinds reset); `OpsEntryValidationTest` (two kinds per day allowed, > 1440 total blocked at submit, note length, sensitive text 422).
stories.benchmark: QuickBooks Time / Toggl are timers built for shifts; neither prefills a weekly placement sheet. Ours: the common case is 'glance, maybe fix Friday, submit'.

stories.title: Flags engine — the full table, settings-keyed tolerances, acknowledgeFlags on approve, bulk approve, proof-required waiver
stories.depsNote: H2.1. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As finance, I want every oddity surfaced and my approval to record which ones I saw, so nothing is corrected silently and the trail holds in a dispute.
stories.genz: Flags, never silent fixes. Approving with a flag means you looked, and it says so.
ac: `OpsFlagService.compute(sheet)` on submit and on approve produces `flags_json` per DESIGN §7: `DAY_OVER_24H` (blocks, 422), `DAY_OVER_WARN` (> setting `org.ops.long_day_hours` 12 h WORK), `TOTAL_NE_EXPECTED` (outside expected ± `org.ops.expected_hours_tolerance_pct` 10), `WEEKEND_WORK`, `OVERLAP_PLACEMENTS` (same consultant, same day, WORK across placements > 1440), `PROOF_MISSING` (placement requires proof and none attached - 409 on submit until H3.2 lands the attachment path; waivable by an approver with audit `OPS_TS_PROOF_WAIVED`), `AFTER_END_DATE`, `CORRECTION`, `INVOICED_SUPERSEDE`; `OCR_MISMATCH`/`OCR_UNREAD` are added by H3.4.

`POST .../approve {acknowledgeFlags: [codes]}` must list every non-info flag present → else 422 `FLAGS_UNACKNOWLEDGED {missing[]}`; acknowledged codes are stored in `decision_flags_json`; `POST /ops/timesheets/approve-bulk {ids[]}` approves only unflagged SUBMITTED sheets and returns `{approved[], skipped[{id, reason}]}`; audit `OPS_TS_APPROVE_BULK` with counts.
Flag codes are the contract: an enum with a `blocks` and `visibleTo` property, exported to the web through the shared `@kiwiply/ui` `FlagChip` copy table.
stories.tests: `OpsFlagsTest` table-driven over every code (tolerance edge, overlap only above 1440, weekend by org week definition, after-end-date); `OpsApproveTest` (unacknowledged 422, bulk skips flagged, waiver audited).
stories.benchmark: Incumbent VMS approvals are a blind 'Approve' button. Ours: 'finance approved 42 h knowing the proof said 40' is on record with a login.

stories.title: Withdraw, correction / supersede chain, locks, DRAFT delete, timeline in the DTO, OPS_READ_SHEET audit
stories.depsNote: H2.2. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want to pull back a submitted week and fix an approved one without support; as finance, I want the old version kept and the invoice told.
stories.genz: Approved is immutable; a fix is a new sheet with a reason that points at the old one.
ac: `POST .../withdraw` SUBMITTED → DRAFT (consultant, own only); `DELETE /ops/timesheets/{id}` DRAFT only (consultant; audited `OPS_TS_DELETE`); `POST .../correct {reason ≤ 300}` from APPROVED creates a new SUBMITTED row with copied entries, `supersedes_id`, `correction_reason`; on approval of the new row the old flips to SUPERSEDED in the same transaction (live_key never collides); the new row may be edited via PUT entries while it is still DRAFT-equivalent (service allows PUT on a correction before its first submit).

`locked_reason = INVOICED` (set by H6.2) still allows correction; the response carries `invoiceNumber` so the UI can say 'This week is on invoice ACME-0007; finance will need to reissue it'; the `INVOICED_SUPERSEDE` flag is set and H6.2's `needs_reissue` hook is called through an interface with a no-op default until H6.2 lands.

`GET /ops/timesheets/{id}` includes `events[]` (the `ops_timesheet_event` timeline incl. who opened it) and `supersedes`/`supersededBy` ids; an approver opening another person's sheet writes `OPS_READ_SHEET` collapsed to one row per actor+target per day.
stories.tests: `OpsTimesheetStateTest` extended (withdraw, delete DRAFT only, correction chain, superseding a locked sheet keeps both readable, concurrent corrections → one 409); `OpsReadAuditTest` (collapse per day).
stories.benchmark: Beeline/Fieldglass corrections after approval need a program-office ticket. Ours: a reason and a resubmit; the old version stays readable.

stories.title: Week view, full UX — long-press numeric entry, weekend collapse, day sheet with kinds, holiday chips, flags confirm, history, PWA
stories.depsNote: H2.3; H0.5 (v0 screen). Size L. Owner web + ui.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want the whole job in one screen that works with my thumb, so a normal week takes 30 seconds.
stories.genz: Prefilled from last week, big steppers, PTO chips, one submit. Done before the elevator arrives.
ac: Week view per DESIGN §3.1: 44 px steppers with long-press opening a numeric sheet; weekend rows collapsed to one tap; day label opens the day sheet (kind chips Work · PTO · Holiday · Sick · Unpaid, minutes, note ≤ 200); 'copied from last week - tap to change' label; holiday chip with the name; 'Copy last week' and 'PTO…' quick actions; total vs expected with the amber soft flag; Submit shows flags first ('Your total is 38 h, expected 40. Submit anyway?') - one-tap confirm except `DAY_OVER_24H`; Withdraw while SUBMITTED; pay line only when the org switch is on.
History list (§3.4): week, client, total, status chip, rejection comment on tap, superseded link; 'Export my sheets (CSV)' calls H0.6.
PWA: the route works installed (existing manifest, mob area) and offline shows the last loaded week read-only with a 'reconnect to submit' note (no offline writes).

`@kiwiply/ui`: `DayKindChips`, `FlagChip` (copy from H2.2's table), `DaySheet`; consented analytics events `ts_week_opened`, `ts_submitted {seconds_open, prefilled, flags}` through `web/src/lib/analytics.ts`.

stories.title: Submit-for by finance (D8, hours only, audited OPS_TS_SUBMIT_FOR) + self-recorded badge for one-person shops (D9)
stories.depsNote: H2.4. Size S. Owner API + web.
stories.story: As finance, I want to close the last week of someone who left mid-week, and as a one-person shop I want to use timesheets at all.
stories.genz: Trailing hours are real. Submitting them for someone is hours, not money, and it says who did it.
ac: `POST /ops/timesheets/{id}/submit-for` (`ops.timesheets.approve`): allowed only when the consultant membership is LEFT/REMOVED/ERASED or the placement is ENDED; submits the DRAFT as-is; audit `OPS_TS_SUBMIT_FOR` with the actor and target; the sheet carries `submitted_for_by_member_id` and the event timeline says 'Submitted by Priya for Aarav'; the approver still cannot self-approve it unless `approval_required=false`.

`ops_settings.approval_required=false` (D9): submit moves straight to APPROVED with `self_recorded=true`; every DTO, the approver list, the PDF pack (H5.2) and CSV exports (H0.6/H5.1) show a visible 'self-recorded' badge/column; the settings UI explains the trade-off; the honest message 'Add a second admin or finance member to approve your own hours, or turn approvals off' appears on `SELF_APPROVAL` 409.
Web: 'Submit for consultant' action on the approver's sheet view only in the allowed states; settings toggle for approvals with the explanation.
stories.tests: `OpsSubmitForTest` (state gate, audit, badge in DTO); `OpsSelfRecordedTest` (approval_required=false path, CSV column present); Playwright for the settings toggle copy.

stories.title: `@NoSensitiveText` + `SensitiveTextValidator` product-wide and `OpsNeverCollectedTest` (schema / DTO / export / enum deny-list gate)
stories.depsNote: H0.7. Relates T1.1 (SensitivePatterns owner) and E10.7 (the same rule in the extension engine). Size M. Owner API. Pure foundation: other areas (O2.5 CSV import, S2.4, U10.1) may adopt the constraint - it stays P2 here because the story is scheduled by this product; say so rather than re-prioritise.
stories.story: As the business, I want it to be impossible - not just forbidden - for this product to collect an SSN/ITIN, bank or routing number, tax id, passport/visa/document number or date of birth.
stories.genz: No field for it, no column for it, no export for it. A policy you can grep, enforced by a failing build.
ac: `api/.../validation/{SensitiveTextValidator,NoSensitiveText}.java` built on the shared `SensitivePatterns` library (T1.1; if T1.1 has not landed, the patterns live here and T1.1 adopts them) with the rules in DESIGN §5.12: SSN/ITIN, EIN, IBAN, Luhn card, 8+ consecutive digits, keyword+number (passport/visa/I-94/I-9/licence/account/routing/tax id), keyword+date (DOB); a `document` mode (9+ digits outside date/time/total context) for scanned text; message 'Don't put account, tax, ID-document numbers or dates of birth here — we never collect them.'; 422 `SENSITIVE_CONTENT`.
`@NoSensitiveText` applied to every String field of every `org/ops` request DTO (H0.3/H1.1/H2.1 interim validators replaced); the constraint is reusable by any area.

`OpsNeverCollectedTest` in the unit suite: (a) no `ops_*` column in Liquibase or JPA matches the deny-list regex; (b) reflection: no DTO field under `org/ops` with a deny-listed name, every String field annotated; (c) `OpsExportColumns` has no deny-listed column in any layout; (d) any `AiSchema` for tasks `OPS_TS_OCR`/`OPS_TS_SCAN` is closed to the enumerated fields (asserted when H3.3/H3.4 register them; the test enumerates registered ops tasks); (e) `pay_type_label` and `method_label` are enums; plus a meta-test proving a deliberately added `ssn` column in the test profile is caught.
A doc↔code test (same pattern as `ShareMatrixTest`, O6.1) asserts the never-collected table in DESIGN §5.12 lists exactly the regex classes.
stories.tests: `SensitiveTextValidatorTest` (every rule, document-mode tolerances for PO/invoice numbers, message snapshot); `OpsNeverCollectedTest` (a–e + meta-test); `OpsNeverCollectedDocTest`.
stories.benchmark: Every incumbent (Ceipal, JobDiva, Bullhorn, Avionté) stores SSNs, I-9s and bank details as core HR data; we are the only one whose timesheets cannot take them - enforced like the consent matrix (O6.1).

stories.title: Proof attachments through `FileStorage` — two-phase upload, caps from entitlements/settings, proxied download, DRAFT-only delete, ledger ref_type
stories.depsNote: H3.1 (the scan hook must exist before the first proof is stored - H3.3 fills it); H2.2 (PROOF_MISSING flag); P5.1 FileStorage local driver - if plat has not started, build on `ResumeStorageService` behind an adapter with the same key shape and swap when P5.1 lands (no table change). Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want to attach the client-approved sheet from my phone and have it stored safely; as the org, I want caps I can configure.
stories.genz: The proof is the record, not an email thread. It lands only after it passed the scan.
ac: Changeset `20261013030000_ts_attachments.xml`: `ops_timesheet_attachment` (DESIGN §5.8), `ops_storage_usage` (§5.11); the `storage_object` ledger (P5.5) gains `ref_type = OPS_ATTACHMENT` and `org_id`.

`POST /ops/timesheets/{id}/attachments` (multipart; consultant own DRAFT/SUBMITTED): bytes go to the FileStorage temp area (`.tmp/<uuid>`, plat D4) and move into place under key prefix `ops-ts` only after `OpsProofScanService.scan()` passes (H3.3; until then a no-op that accepts); sniffed pdf/png/jpg (415 `UNSUPPORTED_FILE`); size ≤ entitlement `ops.attachment_bytes_max` (default 5 MiB; 413 `FILE_TOO_LARGE`); ≤ setting `org.ops.attachments_per_sheet` (3) live per sheet (409 `ATTACHMENT_LIMIT`); org total ≤ entitlement `ops.storage_bytes_max` (default 2 GiB) from `ops_storage_usage` (413 `OPS_STORAGE_CAP`); sha256 stored; `proof_state` → ATTACHED.

`GET .../attachments/{aId}` streams with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, the org permission check and `Range` support from the seam; no presigned URLs anywhere; `DELETE .../attachments/{aId}` only while the sheet is DRAFT; events `ATTACHMENT_ADDED/REMOVED`, audit `OPS_TS_ATTACH/ATTACH_DELETE` with bytes, never content.
`PROOF_MISSING` now resolves against live attachments; `ops_storage_usage` is rebuilt nightly from the ledger (`ops.storage_rebuild` job registered with A10.2 if present, else `@Scheduled`).
stories.tests: `OpsAttachmentIT` on the local driver (temp dir): size boundary at exactly the entitlement, 3-per-sheet, org cap 413 at exactly the cap, PNG named .pdf → 415, DRAFT-only delete, proxied download with permission check, temp file removed on refusal, usage counter rebuilt from the ledger.
stories.benchmark: Ceipal reviewers complain about attachment size limits; no staffing suite we found keeps the client-approved proof inside the sheet. Ours: in-sheet, caps the admin sets.

stories.title: Proof identifier scan + refusal before storage — PDFBox text layer locally, classify-only gateway task `OPS_TS_SCAN` for images, platform safety budget, refused-sha cache
stories.depsNote: H3.2; I0.3 AiGateway (budget owner + task registration). Decision D11 default (a), user may override. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As the business, I want a proof file that shows an SSN, a bank line or a passport number to bounce before it lands, with nothing about it kept but the kinds.
stories.genz: We never held it beyond the temp write. Refusing beats redacting.
ac: `OpsProofScanService.scan(tempRef, contentType)`: PDF with a text layer → PDFBox extraction (already a dependency of resume parsing) + `SensitiveTextValidator` in document mode, no model call; PDF without a text layer, PNG, JPG → `AiGateway` task `OPS_TS_SCAN` with a closed schema `{contains_identifier: bool, kinds: [SSN|BANK|TAX_ID|PASSPORT_VISA|DOB|OTHER_ID], days[], total_minutes, confidence, approver_name?, approved_date?}` (prompt registry id `ops/ts-scan/v1`); the raw model text is discarded; only the hours part is kept and only when the org's OCR is on (H3.4).

Budget: owner = platform safety budget capped at setting `ai.budget.ops_scan_cents_per_consultant` (default 25) × active consultants per period (H1.2's count), counted by the margin guard (B2.1) as the consultant line's worst case together with the OCR budget; when exhausted, image uploads are refused with 422 `SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED {retryAfter}` and the hint 'Try a PDF exported from the client's system' - text-layer PDFs keep working at zero cost.

Detection → 422 `PROOF_HAS_IDENTIFIER {kinds}`; temp file deleted; no ledger row, no attachment row; audit `OPS_TS_PROOF_REFUSED` with kinds only; sha256 of refused bytes cached for setting `org.ops.refused_hash_cache_days` (90) so a re-upload short-circuits; no override path exists (no endpoint, no flag).
`OpsNeverCollectedTest` (d) now asserts the `OPS_TS_SCAN` schema is closed; H6.3 receipts reuse `scan()` unchanged.
stories.tech: `service/org/ops/OpsProofScanService.java` (replaces the H3.2 no-op), `service/ai/AiTask.java` (+ `OPS_TS_SCAN`), prompt registry record `ops/ts-scan/v1` (I2.1 if landed, else `resources/prompts/`), `domain/org/ops/OpsRefusedHash.java` (+ changeset).
stories.tests: `OpsProofScanIT`: hours-only PDF accepted without a gateway call; printed-SSN text-layer PDF refused with nothing stored and a kinds-only audit row; image refused via a stub classifier; budget-exhausted image refused with the PDF alternative; refused-sha short-circuit; cache purge after N days; `OpsNeverCollectedTest` (d) green.
stories.benchmark: Standalone OCR vendors (Lido, Nanonets, Affinda) extract everything on the page; we are the only tool that refuses the page when it carries an identifier.

stories.title: Optional OCR suggestion (off by default, D7) — `OpsOcrService`, closed schema, Ops-grant budget, apply-ocr, `OCR_MISMATCH` / `OCR_UNREAD` flags
stories.depsNote: H3.3. Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant whose org turned it on, I want the hours read from my approved sheet so that nobody re-keys my week; as finance, I want to see when the proof and the hours disagree.
stories.genz: Photo of the approved sheet → hours suggested → you confirm. Never auto-applied.
ac: OCR runs only when `ops_settings.ocr_enabled` (default false) AND entitlement `ops.ocr` (catalog default off) AND (the consultant calls `POST .../attachments/{aId}/read` OR `ops_settings.ocr_auto_read` is true); otherwise `read` → 402 `PLAN_REQUIRED {feature: 'ops.ocr'}` or 409 `OCR_DISABLED`; the gateway task is `OPS_TS_OCR` (prompt `ops/ts-ocr/v1`), budget owner = the org's Ops grant, capped at entitlement `ops.ai_budget_cents_per_consultant` (default 50) × active consultants, pooled per org; exhausted → `ocr_status=SKIPPED`, flag `OCR_UNREAD`, 429 `AI_BUDGET` on an explicit read, submit never blocked.

Response schema closed to `{days:[{date, minutes}], total_minutes, confidence, approver_name?, approved_date?}` validated before `ocr_json` is stored; `approved_date` outside the sheet's week ± setting `org.ops.ocr_approved_date_window_days` (30) is dropped; any extra field rejects the whole result (`ocr_status=FAILED`).

`POST .../apply-ocr {attachmentId}` (DRAFT only) replaces entries with `source=OCR`; `OCR_MISMATCH` when `ocr_total_minutes ≠ work_minutes`, suppressed below setting `org.ops.ocr_min_confidence` (0.6); `proof_state` → READ_MATCH / READ_MISMATCH / READ_FAILED; events `OCR_READ`/`OCR_FAILED`; audit `OPS_TS_OCR_READ` with the summary, never the text.
stories.tests: `OpsOcrTest`: never runs when disabled (the default); gateway stub → suggestion stored; extra field → FAILED; budget exhausted → SKIPPED + flag + submit still allowed; confidence suppression; apply-ocr sets source=OCR and DRAFT-only; `OpsNeverCollectedTest` (d) covers the OCR schema.
stories.benchmark: No staffing suite reads the client-approved proof inside the sheet; OCR vendors sell it separately. Ours: in-sheet, suggestion-only, budget-capped, off until the org asks.

stories.title: Proof UX on the phone — camera capture, client-side downscale, progress and retry, refusal message, OCR Use / Keep (when on)

`@kiwiply/ui`: `ProofTile`, `OcrSuggestion`; analytics event `ts_proof_attached {bytes_bucket, kind, ocr}`.

stories.story: As finance, I want to approve clean sheets in one tap and be made to look at flagged ones with the proof beside the hours.

stories.title: `OpsReminderJob` — consultants with last week missing, approvers with pending, on admin-configured days; quiet hours, daily cap, idempotent per week
stories.depsNote: H4.1; A5.1 settings (the default days/times). Size M. Owner API.
stories.story: As a consultant, I want one reminder when I forget last week; as finance, one when sheets are waiting.
stories.genz: Monday 9 for you, Wednesday 9 for finance, org-local, once per week ever.
ac: Hourly job: for each org with the module on, at `ops_settings.reminder_consultant_dow/time` (defaults from setting `org.ops.reminder_consultant`, MON 09:00) org-local, consultants with an ACTIVE placement and no SUBMITTED/APPROVED sheet for the previous week → `OPS_TS_DUE`; at `reminder_approver_dow/time` (`org.ops.reminder_approver`, WED 09:00) approvers with ≥ 1 SUBMITTED → `OPS_TS_PENDING` with the count.
